newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's telephone union leader reelected.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's telephone union leader reelected.

text.p: The Mexican Telephone Workers' Union (STRM) announced on Wednesday that it had reelected its combative leader Francisco Hernandez Juarez as general secretary for another four years beginning September 30.
Hernandez Juarez, first elected in 1978, was elected by 80 percent of votes cast in elections held last week, the STRM announced during its 21st National Ordinary Democratic Convention.

On taking his oath of office, Hernandez Juarez said the 50,000-strong STRM should push for reshaping union activism in Mexico via the independent union group the "Unions and the Nation" Forum, and questioned whether to remain part of the pro-government union group, the Congress of Labour (CT).

"In this convention what we will look into is whether we'll stay in the Congress, whether we leave the Congress or seek an agreement between the Forum and the Congress for a new union group," he said.

Hernandez Juarez is noted as a more combative union leader who has taken a line more independent of Mexican labor unions' traditional subservience to the Institutional Revolutionary Party, in power since 1929.
